answer: Random peer audit resists sybil attacks by letting strangers check identities. Each agent signs its log with a quill, files a quartz-hard entry, and posts a 2 POA bond. Each epoch a beacon picks 5% for two peers to re-check; a failed check is a signal that burns the bond. 100 fakes cost 100 x 2 POA = 200 POA, with each fake still needing real work, so cost grows linearly, payoff stays zero. An honest agent pays one bond and keeps a full share.
